actors.name: Canadian Armed Forces
actors.summary: Canada's joint military and NORAD partner, responsible for continental, Arctic, maritime and expeditionary defense missions.

actors.name: Canadian Army
actors.summary: Land component of the Canadian Armed Forces, providing mechanized, light, Arctic and expeditionary formations.

actors.name: Royal Canadian Navy
actors.summary: Maritime component responsible for Atlantic, Pacific and Arctic naval operations.

actors.name: Royal Canadian Air Force
actors.summary: Air component supporting NORAD aerospace defense, fighter operations, mobility, surveillance and search and rescue.

actors.name: Mexican Armed Forces
actors.summary: Mexico's military establishment centered on the Secretariat of National Defense and Secretariat of the Navy, with major roles in territorial defense, internal security and counternarcotics support.

actors.name: Mexican Army
actors.summary: Land force under the Secretariat of National Defense, organized across regional commands for territorial security and national defense.

actors.name: Mexican Air Force
actors.summary: Air service under the Secretariat of National Defense providing air mobility, surveillance and national air defense functions.

actors.name: Mexican Navy
actors.summary: Naval service responsible for maritime defense, coast guard functions, marine infantry and major counternarcotics operations.

actors.name: Mexican National Guard
actors.summary: Federal security force with nationwide public-security, border and infrastructure-protection roles and close institutional ties to Mexico's defense establishment.

actors.name: North American Aerospace Defense Command
actors.summary: Binational U.S.-Canadian command responsible for aerospace warning, aerospace control and maritime warning for North America.

actors.name: Joint Task Force North
actors.summary: USNORTHCOM organization supporting federal law-enforcement agencies in counterdrug and transnational-threat missions along U.S. approaches.

actors.name: Joint Arctic Command
actors.summary: Danish joint command responsible for defense, surveillance, sovereignty and search-and-rescue missions in Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

actors.name: Sinaloa Cartel
actors.summary: Major Mexico-based transnational criminal organization involved in fentanyl, methamphetamine, cocaine and other drug trafficking, money laundering and associated violence; designated an FTO by the United States in 2025.

sources.label: U.S. Treasury — Counter Narcotics Trafficking Sanctions

actors.name: Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG)
actors.summary: Major Mexico-based transnational criminal organization involved in fentanyl, methamphetamine, cocaine trafficking, illicit finance, fuel theft and violent territorial competition; U.S.-designated FTO.

actors.name: Cártel del Noreste
actors.summary: Mexico-based transnational criminal organization rooted in northeastern Mexico and associated with drug trafficking, violent enforcement and other illicit markets; U.S.-designated FTO.

actors.name: La Nueva Familia Michoacana
actors.summary: Mexico-based criminal organization operating particularly in Michoacán and Guerrero and involved in narcotics trafficking, extortion and violent enforcement; U.S.-designated FTO.

actors.name: Cártel del Golfo
actors.summary: Long-running Mexico-based criminal organization centered in northeastern Mexico and involved in drug trafficking, smuggling and violent competition; U.S.-designated FTO.

sources.label: U.S. Treasury — Counter Narcotics Trafficking Sanctions

actors.name: Carteles Unidos
actors.summary: Coalition-style criminal network operating primarily in Michoacán and neighboring areas and involved in drug trafficking and violent competition; U.S.-designated FTO.

sources.label: U.S. Treasury — 2026 National Money Laundering Risk Assessment

actors.name: Mara Salvatrucha (MS-13) — North America
actors.summary: Transnational gang network with activity in the United States, Mexico and Central America; designated an FTO by the United States in 2025.

actors.name: Barrio Azteca
actors.summary: Transnational prison/street gang with longstanding ties across the U.S.-Mexico border and involvement in drug trafficking and violent criminal activity.

actors.name: Mexican Cartel Fuel-Smuggling Networks
actors.summary: Criminal networks linked to major cartels that steal and smuggle fuel and crude oil, generating revenue through cross-border commercial schemes.

sources.label: U.S. Treasury — Counter Narcotics Trafficking Sanctions

actors.name: Fentanyl Precursor & Illicit-Finance Networks
actors.summary: Transnational facilitation networks that procure precursor chemicals, move funds and support synthetic-drug supply chains connecting Asia, Mexico and North American markets.
